question: Why don't try-catch blocks in render catch errors thrown by child components? try { return <Child />; } catch (e) { ... }
options: Event handlers and render methods cannot be caught by try-catch, only Error Boundary
try-catch always works in render
Child errors are always handled by Parent try-catch
Error Boundary is the same as try-catch
explanation: try-catch only catches synchronous errors in the try block; render errors from children happen during render phase, caught by Error Boundary, not try-catch.

question: Given a component that throws during render: function Comp() { throw new Error('fail'); }, where is the error caught?
options: Caught by nearest Error Boundary ancestor
Caught by try-catch in parent component
Error propagates to window.onerror
Logged to console, no error boundary needed
explanation: Render-phase errors are caught by Error Boundary using componentDidCatch, not try-catch; Error Boundary must wrap the throwing component.

question: Why does an error in a click handler not get caught by Error Boundary? onClick={() => { throw new Error('fail'); }}
options: Event handlers run outside render phase; Error Boundary doesn't catch them
Error Boundary catches all errors including events
onClick errors are ignored silently
Event errors require try-catch in handler
explanation: Error Boundary only catches render-phase errors; event handlers run after render, so errors must be handled with try-catch or async error handlers.

question: Given componentDidCatch(error, errorInfo), why is errorInfo.componentStack useful?
options: componentStack shows which component threw, useful for debugging render hierarchy
componentStack is a runtime check, no debugging value
componentStack is for logging only
componentStack doesn't provide useful information
explanation: componentStack is a string showing the component tree where the error occurred; it helps identify which component in the hierarchy threw.

question: Why might an Error Boundary not catch an error thrown by a grandchild component?
options: Error Boundary catches all descendants in its tree
Grandchild errors skip the parent Error Boundary
Only immediate children are caught
Error Boundary location doesn't matter
explanation: Error Boundary catches errors from any descendant (child, grandchild, etc.) in its render tree; the closest Error Boundary up the tree handles the error.

question: Given getDerivedStateFromError(error), why must it return new state instead of mutating? return { hasError: true };
options: Must return new state to trigger re-render, mutation doesn't notify React
Mutation and return are equivalent
getDerivedStateFromError doesn't need to return
Only componentDidCatch can return state
explanation: getDerivedStateFromError is pure and must return new state; React re-renders the component with the new state to show fallback UI.

question: Why can't async errors in useEffect be caught by Error Boundary? useEffect(() => { throw new Error('fail'); }, []);
options: useEffect runs after render, errors are not re-render errors, must be caught manually
Error Boundary catches all useEffect errors
useEffect errors are ignored silently
Errors in hooks trigger Error Boundary automatically
explanation: useEffect errors happen after render phase; Error Boundary only catches render-phase errors, so useEffect errors need try-catch or external error handler.

question: Given a custom hook that throws: function useCustom() { if (!condition) throw new Error('fail'); }, where is the error caught?
options: Error Boundary catches errors from any function called during render, including hooks
Hooks are not caught by Error Boundary
Hook errors are caught by try-catch only
Hooks have their own error handling
explanation: Hooks run during render phase; errors thrown from hooks are caught by Error Boundary like any render-phase error.

question: Why might a server-side error in componentDidMount not be caught by Error Boundary?
options: Error Boundary catches render errors, not lifecycle method errors; use try-catch
Error Boundary catches all lifecycle errors
Server errors are global and bypass Error Boundary
componentDidMount errors are always caught
explanation: Error Boundary catches render-phase errors; componentDidMount runs after render, so errors there need try-catch or custom error handling.

question: Given multiple Error Boundaries nested, which boundary catches the error? <ErrorBoundary1><ErrorBoundary2><Child /></ErrorBoundary2></ErrorBoundary1>
options: Nearest Error Boundary (ErrorBoundary2) catches, if it doesn't handle, ErrorBoundary1 catches
ErrorBoundary1 always catches
ErrorBoundary2 always catches
Both catch simultaneously
explanation: Errors are caught by the nearest Error Boundary ancestor; if that boundary doesn't handle it (or re-throws), the next boundary up catches it.
